This is a safe, sensible restart after a week with no runs. It sticks to Nessa's Mon/Wed/Sat schedule and keeps every session an easy walk-run. Saturday adds only one extra interval. Total time is close to her recent ~7 km weeks, so there is no sharp jump and no rushing. Each day is clear enough to run as written. She reported no pain or illness, and the draft rightly doesn't invent any.

Weak points:
- It doesn't ask why all three runs were missed, so the possibility of something like a schedule problem goes unaddressed.
- It never connects the plan to the 15 November 5K goal of running the whole way.
- "The same walk-run that worked two weeks ago" claims a session detail that isn't on the card.
- "Hard-easy spacing" is an odd way to describe an all-easy week.
- It could have mentioned her daily dog walks.

There was no direct question to answer. Overall it's good and safe, but somewhat generic.

── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: 6.8, 7.3, 2.8, 7 km
This week: 0 km over 0 runs. Missed 3 of 3 planned runs.
Body: "All good."
Feeling: "Feeling great, excited for next week."

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: The reviewed week was a zero, so we restart with the same walk-run that worked two weeks ago rather than push into harder running. …
What I read from the week. You wrote that you felt great going in, then no runs landed on Mon, Wed or Sat.
Next week:
Mon: easy, walk-run 24 min, 8 x (2 min run, 1 min walk), flat and conversational…
Tue: rest. Lets the legs settle after the first run back.
Wed: easy, walk-run 24 min, 8 x (2 min run, 1 min walk), same effort as Monday. Repeats…
Thu: rest. Keeps the hard-easy spacing you have been using.
Fri: rest. Protects Saturday's slightly longer session.
Sat: easy, walk-run 27 min, 9 x (2 min run, 1 min walk), flat route. One extra interval…
Sun: rest. A clean day off before next Monday.
